spacetime_coverage.subject: Julia Bowman Robinson
spacetime_coverage.description: Documented places where Julia Robinson lived, studied, carried out research, visited collaborators, or attended meetings. City/district centroids only; intervals of academic affiliation are not proofs of continuous residence; incoming information from Novosibirsk or Soviet publication is not treated as Julia’s travel. The 1975/1976 NAS election discrepancy remains qualified.

places.note: Childhood with family west of Phoenix, twelve miles from the city by Robinson’s recollection; area only. Bounds approximate.
Point Loma from 1925; elementary school and 1928–29 illnesses. Family later moved within San Diego; end date approximate.
Private tutoring and Roosevelt Junior High, then San Diego High School; exact household moves not established.
San Diego State College beginning in 1936; transferred to Berkeley in 1939.
Berkeley transfer 1939; BA 1940, marriage 1941, wartime statistical laboratory, logic study. Interval is a professional base, not continuous location by day.
Raphael’s year at Princeton in 1946–47; Julia pursued general recursive functions.
Returned to Berkeley; PhD completed in 1948 under Alfred Tarski; source appointment period approximate.
Southern California and RAND research environment; worked near UCLA, with this city proxy for RAND base, not a claim about daily residence.
International Congress of Mathematicians at Harvard, where Robinson met Martin Davis.
Long-term base for Hilbert’s tenth work, 1952 existential definitions and DPR 1961 work; not continuous physical presence.
Met Yuri Matiyasevich at the 1971 Fourth International Congress for Logic, Methodology and Philosophy of Science.
Documented 1971 visit with Raphael and meeting with Yuri and Nina Matiyasevich; not the 1970 proof discovery location by Julia.
Berkeley research, 1975 Academy election (reported), full professorship 1976, AMS presidency 1983–84; not proof of presence at all institutional events.
AMS summer meeting where she learned of her leukemia, according to Constance Reid.
Bicycling with sister Constance while memoir was discussed in 1985; precise private route not claimed.
Died on 30 July 1985; Constance drafted biography and read it to Julia during medical treatment.
